title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes a combinatorial or ordered setting for topology. An 'atelier' (workshop) is a set F of 'figures' carrying an order ≤ and a 'well-inside' relation ≪, subject to axioms At 1–At 7. The model example is Fig(M), the atelier of figures in a space M. On the previous page a sub-atelier F' ⊂ F is defined as (Sousat 1) a non-empty closed part of (F, ≤), i.e. a down-closed subset, such that (Sousat 2) F' with the induced ≤ and ≪ is again an atelier. Sousat 2 is a condition on the existence of joins X ∨ Y inside F'.

This page does four things.
(1) Definition: F' is a 'sous-atelier spacieux' (spacious sub-atelier) if it is a 'spacious' closed part of F. Grothendieck notes that this already implies F' is a sub-atelier: spaciousness forces Sousat 2. 'Spacious' was defined earlier (pp. 21, 27), presumably a lower set that is saturated or cofinal with respect to ≪ or joins.
(2) Example: for an atelier F there is a canonical map F → Fig(M). He recalls that its image is closed (down-closed) for ≤, and that ≤ and ≪ on F are induced from Fig(M). Hence every atelier is a sub-atelier of the atelier of figures of its associated M. This is a representation or realization statement.
(3) The image is in general NOT spacious. He leaves open whether it is spacious in the 'ensembliste' (set-theoretic) case: 'à voir'.
(4) Remark: for a poset F and a non-empty lower set F', the non-empty lower sets of F' are exactly the non-empty lower sets of F contained in F'. The same holds for spacious closed parts provided F' itself is spacious. The next page makes this precise as a transitivity statement: for F'' ⊂ F' ⊂ F, if F'' is spacious in F' it is spacious in F, with the converse when F' is spacious in F. It then gives formulas (1,50) and (1,51) describing sub-ateliers and spacious sub-ateliers of F' as those of F contained in F'.

Purpose: to set up the lattice of sub-objects (sub-ateliers) of a combinatorial model of space. This is presumably preparation for gluing and localization, playing a role like opens in a site or locale.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The general-poset statement about lower sets is trivially correct.
The transitivity claim for 'spacious' cannot be checked without the definition from pp. 21/27, but it is the expected kind of statement.
The question of whether the image of F in Fig(M) is spacious in the set-theoretic case is left open on this page.

ideas.what: Sub-atelier: a non-empty down-closed subset of an ordered 'workshop' with a well-inside relation, closed under the relevant joins, which is again an atelier.
ideas.modern_name: Sub-object / ideal-like sub-structure of a proximity lattice or abstract basis (cf. continuous posets with way-below relation, strong proximity lattices)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Domain theory and pointless topology: Scott, Smyth, Jung–Sünderhauf (proximity lattices, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; tame topology is only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Canonical embedding of an atelier F into the atelier Fig(M) of figures of its 'space' M, with image down-closed and ≤, ≪ induced. Every atelier is thus a sub-atelier of a concrete one.
ideas.modern_name: Representation theorem (Stone-type realization of an abstract basis or proximity structure by figures in a space)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone-duality tradition; for proximity lattices, Smyth / Jung–Sünderhauf

ideas.what: Lower sets of a lower set; transitivity of 'spacious' closed parts.
ideas.modern_name: Transitivity of sieves / down-sets; the induced sub-poset of sub-objects

missed.claim: Open question whether the canonical image of an atelier in Fig(M) is a spacious sub-atelier in the set-theoretic case.
missed.quote: Mais ce n'est pas en général sous-atelier spacieux (mais ça l'est peut-être dans le cas ensembliste, à voir).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small open point inside an unpublished axiomatization of tame topology. It matters only to someone reconstructing Grothendieck's 'ateliers' as a framework, e.g. in comparison with proximity lattices or o-minimal structures.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine bookkeeping on sub-structures (sub-ateliers, spacious parts) inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework itself, an ordered-set approach to analysis situs with a well-inside relation, is little known, but this page adds only definitions and trivial lemmas plus one small open question.
transcription_corrections: 'sous-atlas' should read 'sous-atelier' throughout; likewise 'atlas' should read 'atelier' ('Soit F un atelier', 'l'atelier des figures dans M').

In the Remarque, 'partie finie' should read 'partie fermée' throughout: '... F' une partie fermée non vide de F. Alors les parties fermées non vides de F' sont exactement les parties fermées non vides de F ...', and 'parties fermées spacieuses'.

The first line reads 'F' est un sous-atelier spacieux, si c'est une partie fermée spacieuse de F'. The struck text is 'Lorsque la condition Sousat 2 est', followed by 'Ce qui suffit à entraîner que c'est un sous-atelier.'
Struck line: 'En fait, on a vu aussi qu'il est un' (correct). 'Mais ce n'est pas en général' is inserted above.
On the next page, 'opposition [?]' is likely 'spacieux', and 'ensemble/sous-ensemble [?]' and 'Sousens' are likely 'atelier/sous-atelier' and 'Sousat'.
